title: Tupaia's chart of the Pacific
summary: Tupaia, an arioi priest and master navigator from Raʻiātea, drew a chart of the Pacific islands in 1769-70 together with members of the crew of James Cook's Endeavour, which he joined at Tahiti in July 1769. Researchers at the University of Potsdam argue it shows interconnected voyaging paths from roughly Samoa to Rapa Nui and from the Society Islands to Hawaiʻi.

uncertainty.note: Both sources give a span, 1769/1770 and circa 1769-70, not a single day. Tupaia joined the Endeavour at Tahiti in July 1769 and died in Jakarta on 11 November 1770 (Natural History Museum).

as_recorded.value: drawn by Tupaia ... in collaboration with various members of the crew of James Cook's Endeavour in 1769/1770
Chart showing the Pacific Islands, based on information provided by Tupaia ... circa 1769-70

where.modern_name: Raʻiātea, Leeward Society Islands, French Polynesia (Tupaia's home island); the chart was drawn aboard Endeavour
where.historical_name: Raʻiātea, Society Islands (Tahiti and neighbouring islands)

importance.justification: A chart of Pacific islands that translated Polynesian wayfinding knowledge for the Endeavour crew, and that scholars say shows voyaging paths over a very large region.

reviewer_note: Pin marks Tupaia's home island, not the place of drawing (aboard ship, location unrecorded on opened pages). The reading of the chart is the Eckstein and Schwarz interpretation named by the University of Potsdam page; the identity of many islands is described there as a long-standing riddle. The island count of the chart differs across sources (not stated here). Tupaia's spelling and Raʻiātea follow the sources.
